headline: China Activates World's Largest Offshore Wind Turbine Cluster
meta_description: China has switched on a 2 GW offshore wind project in the South China Sea with 131 turbines, marking a major renewable energy milestone.
summary_short: A massive offshore wind farm with 131 turbines, including 33 giant 18 MW units, is now generating clean power in the South China Sea.
body:
China has switched on the world's largest cluster of 18 MW offshore wind turbines in the South China Sea, marking a major renewable energy milestone. The 2 GW project harnesses wind power at unprecedented scale in a single installation.

The facility comprises 131 turbines in total, with 33 of them representing the giant 18 MW class—the largest capacity turbines in this coordinated cluster. Once fully operational, the project is expected to generate 6.6 billion kilowatt-hours annually, delivering substantial clean energy to meet growing demand across the region.

This development reflects growing momentum in offshore wind technology, where larger individual turbines and densely packed installations are becoming increasingly viable. The South China Sea project demonstrates how advanced engineering can unlock renewable resources in challenging marine environments, offering a replicable model for other coastal nations pursuing decarbonization goals.
